newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy says profits fall fourth quarter earnings.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy says profits fall fourth quarter earnings.

text.p: Consumer electronics retailer Best Buy Co. Inc. said Wednesday its profits fell sharply in the latest quarter due to tough competition and a changing mix of products at its stores.

Earnings for the fiscal fourth quarter ended March 1 fell to $8.5 million, or 20 cents per share, from $19.8 million, or 46 cents share, in the year ago quarter. Sales fell to $2.3 billion from $2.6 billion.
Profits for the full fiscal year dropped to $1.7 million, or 4 cents per share, from $48 million, or $1.10 per share, in the prior fiscal year.
While the profits were down sharply, they still exceeded analysts expectations that the retailer would just break even for the year.
"A challenging retail environment overshadowed our progress on several key initiatives to increase profitability," said Chairman Richard Schulze.

Sales were up 8 percent in fiscal 1997 to $7.7 billion above last year's $7.2 billion, but Best Buy said comparable store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year, declined 5 percent due to weak industry environment.
The company said it had taken steps to improve future profit margins by foscusing on more profitable merchandise and lowering inventories of some merchandise.

Best Buy also said that it expects sales will decline in the first half of this fiscal year, resulting in a loss for the first six months because of continuing soft sales in some categories of merchandise.

The company said, however, it expects an improvement in gross profit percentages because of growth in the sales of performance service plans, planning improvements and increased marketing effectiveness.
Best Buy said its financial position has improved, compared to the prior year-end, as inventories are about $70 million lower including the addition of 21 new stores.
